title: Author src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md — the add-a-set recipe, written BEFORE any plant-products file exists (R6 / G-A)
recipe: This increment WRITES a recipe; it does not follow one. Its form is dictated by the existing recipe corpus — read src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md and add-a-collection.md FIRST and match their voice, heading style and step shape exactly. Its content is distilled from SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §8 G-A (the 10 required steps), §4.1-§4.6 (the co-residency mechanism, the symmetric `'/' + setId` mount scheme and the enumerated live-animals URL migration), §10 (the tests-repo half), §1 (the m0 file list and exports), §6.2 (records port incl. the Idempotency-Key copy contract) and §7 (test scaffolding + verification ladder).

filesToTouch.what:
The add-a-set recipe. LOCATION IS LOAD-BEARING: it goes in the L1/platform docs dir alongside architecture.md, persistence.md and engine.md — NOT under sets/live-animals/docs/ (a set-level doc cannot own a cross-set procedure; SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-A states this explicitly). FORM: match sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md — an opening sentence saying when to use it and when not to, a 'Run every command from the frontend repo root' path-convention paragraph, a 'Read these files first' section listing concrete relative-link exemplars, then numbered '## N. <imperative step>' sections, each with the exact file/export/edit to make, then a verification section. GDS plain English, second person, no marketing. CONTENT — the ten steps of §8 G-A, restated for co-residency:

1. '## 1. Choose the set name and its mount prefix' — the co-residency contract stated plainly: BOTH gateways register in ONE Node process; every configure* seam is keyed by set id; a request resolves its set from the OWNING PLUGIN REALM, never by parsing the URL (FD-1/FD-14/FD-15). State the SYMMETRIC MOUNT rule (R7 — this REPLACES the reversed FD-16 wording; do not write 'the incumbent set keeps the root, a new set takes a prefix' anywhere in this file): **the mount prefix is NOT a choice — it is `'/' + setId`.** Every set mounts under its own prefix; NO set is ever registered at prefix '' and `registerSetMount` throws if one is passed. Give the reasoning in two lines: the set id is already the key for every other per-set fact (setKeyed, withSetContext, the plugin name, the cookie-name prefix, the sets/<setId>/ dir, the Nunjucks TEMPLATES root, the dep-cruiser regexes, the npm scripts, the Playwright project names), so deriving the mount from it means one fact per set and no mount table to drift; and with no set at '' a doubled prefix and a dropped prefix both fail visibly on the first request instead of producing the same correct-looking string for whichever set sat at the root. Then state the two consequences the author must not discover later: (a) FD-18 — `/` belongs to NO set; it is a server-wide 302 (never 301) to the default set's dashboard, declared with `server.route` in src/server/router.js behind a single DEFAULT_SET_BASE constant, OUTSIDE both gateways, so it never enters a set context and never appears in any set's allRoutes; (b) FD-19 — `/health`, `/signout`, the `/auth/*` OIDC routes and the static-asset route (`${assetPath}/{param*}`) are SERVER-WIDE and must NEVER sit inside a prefixed `server.register` call. Call out that signout is the live trap: it registers perfectly well at `/live-animals/signout` and nothing fails until a user tries to sign out, so it gets its own unprefixed register call and its own assertion. Include the mount table shape (set | prefix | dashboard | create | hub | page) with both sets filled in, and name the P-11 symmetry tripwire (src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js) here as well as in step 4 — it fails the build if a set is registered at '' or at anything other than '/' + setId. Cite §4.3 and §4.6.

2. '## 2. Create the L3 skeleton' — sets/<name>/obligations/index.js with `export const obligations = []`, the DERIVED groups formula copied verbatim from sets/live-animals/obligations/index.js (never hand-kept), and the `policy` export shape from P-1: `{ systemPopulated: [], enforcedAtContinue: [], maxEntriesFrom: {}, systemAnswerKeys: ['referenceNumber'] }`. State the rule that obligation names are camelCase, path-safe (no dots or brackets) or buildDispatch throws at boot, and carry NO display text.

3. '## 3. Create the L4 skeleton' — sets/<name>/journeys/linear/: config.js (TEMPLATES = '<name>/journeys/linear', LAYOUT = 'shared/layout.njk' unprefixed, and THREE SET-PREFIXED SESSION_COOKIE_NAMES — say explicitly that under co-residency these names are load-bearing, not cosmetic, because both sets' cookies live in the same browser at the same time); flow/flow.js (FLOW_ONLY_KEYS, sections, derived allFlowPages/sectionOfPage/answerSections); flow/task-rows.js (taskRows, rowStatus delegating to L2 bridge/status); flow/run.js (RUN_STEPS, nextRunTarget); flow/entry-guard.js (entryGuardTarget); features/index.js (dispatchPages, allRoutes); features/evaluation.js (featureEvaluationBindings = Object.freeze([])). Name the exact export names each file must have for configureJourneyFlow / buildDispatch to accept it.

4. '## 4. Write the L1 gateway' — the call table with the LOAD-BEARING ORDER: context → mount → config → assertions → dispatch → persistence → cookies → guard → priming → routes. Spell out: `registerSetMount(setId, '/' + setId)` — written that way, so the symmetry is in the code rather than in a convention someone has to remember; server.ext('onPreAuth', …enterSetContext(setId)…) as the FIRST thing in the register body; the whole body wrapped in `await withSetContext(setId, async () => { … })` because assertObligationPurity/assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage/buildDispatch read through currentSetId() outside any request; setId as the FIRST argument of configureObligationSet / configureFulfilmentRegistry / configureJourneyFlow / buildDispatch / configureRecords / configureSession; `registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/' + setId, cookieNames })` — again written with the derivation visible — so the three session cookies are path-scoped to the set's own subtree and one set's draft is invisible to another; which seams are OPTIONAL (configureCommodityReference — only the L2 live-animals mapper consumes it, so a set that owns its own records service never calls it and its slot is provably absent); when priming applies (countries.prime()/ports.prime() are live-animals-mode machinery and run on that gateway only — a fixture-backed set primes nothing). Point at the P-11 tripwire test (src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js) by name for BOTH of its rules, so the author meets them BEFORE writing the file: the setId-first seam rule AND the R7 symmetry rule (no set at '', every prefix exactly '/' + setId).

5. '## 5. Register the gateway' — add it to the routes.js barrel (`export { <name> } from './routes-<name>.js'`) and register it in src/server/router.js with its OWN `await server.register(<name>, { routes: { prefix: '/<name>' } })` call. Show the shape as ONE PREFIXED REGISTER CALL PER SET, one line each, plus the hoisted unprefixed `if (authEnabled) await server.register([signout])` and the `GET /` 302 route — i.e. show what the whole block looks like with two sets in it, not just the line being added. Say why each part is the way it is: `routes.prefix` applies to a WHOLE register call, so two sets can never share one; signout must not be in an array with a set gateway (FD-19) or it silently moves under that set's prefix; and the `/` redirect uses `server.route`, not a gateway, so it stays out of every set context (FD-18).

6. '## 6. Edit dependency-cruiser' — add the new gateway file to the routes-is-the-gateway pathNot allowlist and to the sets-not-l1 forbidden-target regex (sets must not import ANY routes-*.js). State the baseline rule loudly: do NOT regenerate .dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json to absorb anything.

7. '## 7. Add the test scaffolding' — the set-scoped Vitest script (`test:<name>`), the per-set Playwright project (testDir at the set's features dir, same use block, specs navigating under the set's prefix), the cloned app-root suites (contract / routes / indexed / store-ops / one-load-per-request as *.<name>.test.js — each composes ONE set so the sole-set fallback means they need no context plumbing), the empty contract table with harness and zero cases, and A NEW CASE IN co-residency.test.js. Say that the parameterised fs-walk convention tests (copy-convention, copy-parity) loop over set roots in-file and need the new root added.

THEN A CROSS-REPO CLAUSE (R8 — the half that was missing from the plan entirely): **a set is not done when its in-repo tests pass.** The in-repo *.e2e.spec.js suites run against a self-hosted server on the records STUB; only repos/trade-imports-animals-tests runs the same journeys against the real workspace stack — real backend, real Mongo, real OIDC. So the recipe requires, in that repo and on the SAME branch name (CLAUDE.md rule 2): page objects under page-objects/<set-id>/ extending the set-aware NotificationPage with the set's base from page-objects/base/sets.ts; a flow under flows/<set-id>/; per-set specs under tests/{a11y,e2e/features,e2e/pages,e2e/journeys}/<set-id>/; a Playwright project frontend-<set-id>-chromium in utils/playwright/shared-config.ts, testMatch-scoped to that subtree and mapped to the SAME frontend base URL as every other set (the base URL is HOST-ONLY — a set-prefixed base URL breaks /signout, /health, assets and the OIDC callback and makes the other sets unreachable); and the project name added to every playwright.*.config.ts project list, to package.json's script flags and to the CI workflows, or CI silently stops running a whole set. Cite §10 (and §10.2 for the layer-by-layer parameterise-vs-clone ruling: one set-aware URL layer, two of everything above it).

8. '## 8. Stand up the set services' — mode switch (<NAME>_MODE, stub|real, default real); the records adapter against the set's own backend surface, presented as an engine-port-op → HTTP table (the 11 ops: create, load, list, has, replaceFulfilment, finalise, amend, cancelAmend, copy, softDelete, clear) INCLUDING THE Idempotency-Key CONTRACT FOR copy — a randomUUID() minted per RENDERED copy action, carried in a hidden input named idempotencyKey, sent as the Idempotency-Key request header by the real adapter, mirrored by a dedupe key in the stub, with records-port contract tests pinning 'one new draft per idempotency key' and 'copy idempotency scoped to the source reference'; reference-data fixtures. State the mapper omission discipline: a field with no backend home gets an explicit omission assertion, never an invented payload property.

9. '## 9. Build the minimum usable surfaces' — dashboard, hub (+ GROUPS), entry filter, entry-guard policy. Warn that the set's entry guard must derive its journey prefix from a FUNCTION (setBase()-derived), never a module-load const — name the live-animals JOURNEY_PREFIX bug class as the reason.

10. '## 10. Verify — the two-sided, co-residency ladder' — every set already in the tree AND the new set must serve correctly FROM ONE RUNNING PROCESS. The ladder: baseline `npm run test:<name>` before editing; then `npm run test:<name>`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `PORT=3050 npm run test:features:<name>`, `npm run test:features:all` (one server, both projects), `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run format`. co-residency.test.js must be green and must have gained a case for the new set — including that GET `/<name>` serves the new set, GET `/` still 302s to the default set, and `/signout`, `/health` and the static-asset route still resolve UNPREFIXED now that another prefixed register exists. THEN THE TESTS-REPO LEG (R8), which is part of the ladder and not an optional extra: on the same branch name, run the workspace E2E suite from repos/trade-imports-animals-tests against a co-resident stack — `npm run test:live-animals` and `npm run test:<name>` there, plus the full suite — and confirm both frontend Playwright projects are discovered by `playwright test --list`. State explicitly that the retired bar was 'the new set is green AND the default set is unchanged under its own env', and the current bar is 'EVERY set serves correctly from the same running process, proven in-repo by co-residency.test.js and test:features:all AND cross-repo by the tests-repo suite against the real stack'.

Close with a short '## What this recipe does not cover' section pointing at the remaining gaps by name (depth-3 nested collections, hub-from-scratch, check-answers-from-scratch, flow-only keys, CSV branch) so a future author does not assume coverage.

specs: NONE — documentation-only increment, no runnable spec. The recipe's correctness is proved downstream: every m0-b scaffold increment (pp-007 and its siblings) cites the add-a-set.md step it is executing, and any step that cannot be followed verbatim is a defect in THIS increment, fixed here rather than worked around in the scaffold.
acceptanceCriteria: src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md exists at the L1/platform docs level (alongside architecture.md), NOT under sets/live-animals/docs/.

The recipe contains all ten steps of SIBLING-SET-PLAN §8 G-A as numbered sections, in order, each stating a concrete file/export/edit rather than a principle: (1) set name + the SYMMETRIC mount rule (prefix = '/' + setId, no set at '') + the co-residency contract + FD-18 (`/` is a server-wide 302 to the default set) + FD-19 (health/signout/auth/static are server-wide and never inside a prefixed register); (2) L3 obligations skeleton incl. the derived-groups formula and the policy export shape; (3) L4 skeleton with the exact required exports per file and the load-bearing set-prefixed cookie names; (4) the L1 gateway call table with load-bearing order, setId-first, withSetContext, onPreAuth, registerSetMount, per-set registerJourneyCookie, optional seams and priming; (5) routes.js barrel + ONE PREFIXED router.js register call PER SET, shown with the hoisted unprefixed signout register and the `/` 302 in the same block; (6) dep-cruiser edits without touching the violations baseline; (7) test scaffolding incl. a co-residency.test.js case AND the cross-repo clause (page objects, flow, per-set specs and a Playwright project in repos/trade-imports-animals-tests, on the same branch name, with a host-only base URL); (8) set services incl. the records op→HTTP table and the Idempotency-Key copy contract; (9) minimal usable surfaces; (10) the co-residency verification ladder INCLUDING the tests-repo leg.

R7 WORDING CHECK: the phrase 'the incumbent set keeps the root' (and any variant asserting a root-mounted set) appears NOWHERE in the file — `grep -rn "root mount\|keeps the root\|prefix ''" src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md` returns nothing except, at most, an explicit statement that no set is mounted at ''.
The file names src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js in BOTH step 1 (the symmetry rule) and step 4 (the setId-first rule), and cites §4.3, §4.6 and §10 of SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md.

Step 7's cross-repo clause and step 10's tests-repo leg both name repos/trade-imports-animals-tests explicitly and both state the same-branch-name requirement (CLAUDE.md rule 2). A reader following this recipe cannot finish a set without touching that repo.

The recipe reads as a sibling of sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md: same second-person imperative voice, same 'Run every command from the frontend repo root' path convention, a 'Read these files first' section of concrete relative links, numbered imperative step headings, no marketing language and no restatement of rationale that belongs in SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md (cite it instead).

Every file path, export name and function signature named in the recipe matches the target seam shapes specified in SIBLING-SET-PLAN §4.1/§4.2/§4.3 (withSetContext, enterSetContext, currentSetId, currentSetBase, registerSetMount, setKeyed, setBase, pageRoutePath/hubRoutePath/dashboardRoutePath/createRoutePath, registerJourneyCookie(server, { base, cookieNames })) — the shapes pp-056 and pp-057 implement.
The recipe names the P-11 tripwire test (src/server/app/no-set-singletons.test.js) in step 4 so a gateway author meets the setId-first rule before writing the file.

Step 8 states the Idempotency-Key copy contract in full — per-rendered-action randomUUID(), hidden idempotencyKey input, Idempotency-Key request header in the real adapter, dedupe key in the stub, and the two records-port contract assertions — so no future set ships a Copy button without it.

Step 10 states the CURRENT verification bar ('every set serves correctly from the same running process, proven in-repo AND cross-repo against the real stack') and explicitly records that the old bar ('the new set is green and the default set is unchanged under its own env') is retired. No mention of SERVED_SET or any served-set env var appears anywhere in the file.
The doc is markdown-lint/prettier clean under npm run format and npm run lint; internal relative links resolve to files that exist today.
No source file is edited — the new markdown file is the entire diff.
notes:
AMENDED FOR RULINGS R7 AND R8 (Sam, 2026-08-01, later session). R7 — SYMMETRIC MOUNTS, FD-16 reversed: step 1's content is REWRITTEN. The sentence the round-2 recipe was to contain — 'the incumbent set keeps the root mount, every new set takes a prefix' — is deleted and must not reappear in any form. In its place: the mount prefix is not a choice, it is `'/' + setId`; no set owns `/`; `/` is a server-wide 302 to the default set (FD-18); and `/health`, `/signout`, `/auth/*` and the static-asset route are server-wide and must never sit inside a prefixed `server.register` call (FD-19, with signout named as the live trap because it registers happily at the wrong path). Step 4 now shows `registerSetMount(setId, '/' + setId)` and `registerJourneyCookie(server, { base: '/' + setId, cookieNames })` with the derivation visible in the code, and points at P-11's SYMMETRY tripwire as well as its setId-first one. Step 5 shows one prefixed register call per set PLUS the hoisted unprefixed signout register and the `/` redirect, as a whole block rather than a single added line. R8 — TESTS-REPO COVERAGE: step 7 gains a cross-repo clause (a set is not done until it has page objects, a flow, per-set specs and a Playwright project in repos/trade-imports-animals-tests, on the same branch name, with a HOST-ONLY base URL) and step 10's ladder gains the tests-repo leg. The file now cites §4.3, §4.6 and §10.

WHY THIS IS FIRST (Sam's ruling R6, 2026-08-01): round 1 said 'this plan IS the recipe; extracting docs/add-a-set.md afterwards is a recommended m4+ chore'. R6 reverses that. The recipe is authored BEFORE any sets/plant-products/ file exists and the m0 scaffold increments then FOLLOW it verbatim, exactly as the frontend-change skill follows add-a-field.md / add-a-page.md / add-a-collection.md. Writing it first is what closes gap G-A; extracting it afterwards would only document whatever happened to be built.

HEADLESS DECISION — dependsOn is [] (the orchestrator's explicit instruction: 'it is FIRST, before all m0 work'). This differs from SIBLING-SET-PLAN §9 step 7, which sequences the recipe AFTER P-9/P-10 so it can describe the seams 'as they actually are'. Recording the tension and the resolution: the recipe is authored against the TARGET seam shapes that §4.1/§4.2/§4.3 specify and that pp-056 (P-9) and pp-057 (P-10) implement. Because those sections specify the shapes down to function names and signatures, a doc written from them is not speculative — but it IS unverified against running code until the platform increments land. Mitigation, and it is mandatory: the implementor of pp-056, pp-057 and pp-006 must re-read add-a-set.md at the end of their increment and correct any drift between the doc and the seams they actually shipped. If a platform increment finds it cannot ship the shape the recipe describes, the recipe is wrong and gets fixed in that increment — the recipe is not allowed to rot into aspiration.

EXEMPLARS (read before writing, in this order): src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-page.md (the closest match for step shape and voice), src/server/app/sets/live-animals/docs/add-a-collection.md (the longest recipe — shows how a multi-file procedure is broken into steps), src/server/app/docs/architecture.md (the L1/platform doc voice and the neighbours this file joins), src/server/app/docs/README.md (the docs index — add the new file to it if it enumerates the platform docs).

SOURCE SECTIONS to distil (cite by heading, do not paste wholesale): §8 G-A (the ten steps), §4.1 (shared/set-context.js — the module listing gives the exact export names), §4.2 (the per-seam table — rows 1-11 give the exact configure*/accessor names), §4.3 (route-shape vs link builders, the REWRITTEN `'/' + setId` mount scheme and mount table — note the 'live-animals URLs do not change' rule is RETIRED by R7), §4.6 (the enumerated live-animals URL migration, which is what the symmetric scheme cost once), §10 (the tests-repo strategy the step-7 cross-repo clause and the step-10 ladder leg come from), §4.4.3 (the 14-row gateway call table with the load-bearing order), §4.4.4-5 (barrel + router registration), §1 (the m0 file list and every file's required exports), §6.2 (the op→HTTP table and the R4 Idempotency-Key copy row), §7 (T-1..T-10 and the plant verification ladder), §5 P-4 (dep-cruiser edits), §5 P-11 (the tripwire).

SCOPE FENCE: this increment writes ONE markdown file. It does not create sets/plant-products/, does not edit dep-cruiser, does not touch playwright.config.js or package.json. Anything that would change behaviour belongs to pp-056/pp-057/pp-058/pp-006/pp-007.
